text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- The Coalition Party decided to support Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi and to continue an investigation into alleged shady deals with the privatisation of appartments in central Tallinn. The opposition still plans a vote of no-confidence.

- The opposition Reform Party MP Daimar Liiv claimed that the Council of Europe commission members were interested in suspicions about Vaehi's link to the appartments affair as well as suspected insider dealing with Union Bank shares.
- The trade unions central confederation accuses the government of failing to take measures to raise minimum salaries.
- Foreign minister Toomas Hendrik Ilves visited Latvia and stressed the importance of cooperation at his meetings with the president, the premier and foreign minister.
- Swedish foreign aid minister Pierre Schori promised that visa-free travel between Sweden and Estonia would most probably be started before summer.
- The national art museum has not recovered the 3.8 million kroons worth of art works stolen approximately two years ago although the thieves have been caught and a trial is in progress.
- A former owner demands the return or compensation for the land on which the main Savings Bank office building is currently being built.
- Tallinn council financial advisor admits that the city has no clear idea how to use approximately 40 million kroons out of the 480 million kroon Nomura loan.
